PRIVACY & COOKIE POLICY

Last updated: 25 August 2026

This Policy explains how Photon Digital processes personal data when you use the website, contact us, book a meeting, or interact with us as a client. It also describes the use of cookies, Cookiebot, Google Consent Mode v2 and Calendly.

1. Who we are and who controls the data

The website https://photon-digital.com/ and the Photon Digital brand are operated by Ukrainian sole proprietor (FOP) Кузьменюк Борис Олександрович (the “Controller”, “Photon Digital”, “we”, “us”).

Ukrainian Unified State Register record No. 2011600000000096423, registered on 17 August 2026.

Registered address: 21 Striletska Street, Vinnytsia, Vinnytsia District, Vinnytsia Region, 21007, Ukraine.

Privacy contact: info@photon-digital.com. Website: https://photon-digital.com/. Phone: +38 (068) 708-32-41.

Photon Digital is the controller for personal data used to operate its own website, handle enquiries, enter into and perform contracts, manage client relationships and comply with legal obligations.

When we access or process personal data in a client’s advertising, analytics, CRM or other systems solely on the client’s documented instructions, Photon Digital may act as a processor/service provider and the client remains the controller. Those activities should be governed by the relevant services agreement and, where required, a Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

2. Scope of this Policy

This Policy applies to website visitors, people who submit a form or email us, people who book a meeting, prospective and current clients, and other business contacts.

It describes processing performed by Photon Digital for its own purposes. Where we process data on behalf of a client, the client’s instructions and the applicable contract primarily govern that processing.

3. Personal data we may collect

3.1. Data you provide directly

through the website form: your name, email address, message and any additional information you choose to include;

when booking through Calendly: your name, email address, selected date and time, time zone, booking-form answers and other information you voluntarily provide;

in correspondence: contact details, message content and attachments;

during a client relationship: name, role, company, contact, contractual and billing/accounting details, project information, and access details for advertising or analytics systems to the extent necessary to provide the services.

3.2. Technical and analytics data

IP address, approximate location, browser and version, device, operating system, language, URL and referrer, date/time of requests and technical security logs;

page views and interactions, cookie/local-storage identifiers, advertising identifiers or click IDs (for example gclid) where applicable;

cookie consent choices and Consent Mode signals.

3.3. Data from other sources

information made available through Google Analytics, Google Ads and other advertising/analytics platforms according to their settings;

information supplied by a client or its authorised personnel for the performance of our services;

business contact information from public business sources or referrals where permitted by law.

3.4. Special-category data

We do not ask you to submit health data, biometric data, political or religious beliefs, sexual-life data, criminal-conviction data or other sensitive information through the website. Please do not include such information in free-text fields or Calendly unless it is strictly necessary.

4. Purposes and legal bases

The specific legal basis depends on the context. For individuals in the EEA/UK we refer to the relevant GDPR/UK GDPR basis; Ukrainian data-protection law also applies to our activities in Ukraine.

5. Cookies, Cookiebot and Google Consent Mode v2

We use Cookiebot CMP by Usercentrics to manage cookie consent. The banner allows visitors to allow all cookies, choose categories, or reject non-essential cookies. Categories may include Necessary, Preferences, Statistics and Marketing.

Non-essential cookies and storage should not be activated until the relevant consent is given. You can change or withdraw your choice at any time through Cookie Settings / the Cookie Declaration on the website.

The website uses Google Consent Mode v2 in Advanced mode. Before the user makes a choice, the relevant consent states are configured as denied. In Advanced mode, Google tags may load and send limited cookie-free measurements (“cookieless pings”) together with the consent state. While analytics_storage or ad_storage remains denied, analytics/advertising cookies should not be read or written. After consent is granted, Google may receive fuller measurement data according to the categories you allowed.

Consent Mode includes, among other signals, analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization.

The current list of cookies/trackers, providers, purposes and retention periods is shown in the dynamic Cookie Declaration generated by Cookiebot. This is the primary source for cookie-specific details because it updates as the website is rescanned.

6. Service providers and recipients

We disclose personal data only to the extent needed for the relevant purpose and use contractual/technical safeguards where applicable. Key categories of recipients are listed below.

7. International transfers

Photon Digital is established in Ukraine, while some infrastructure and service providers operate in the EEA, the United States and other countries. Personal data may therefore be processed outside the country where you are located.

Where GDPR/UK GDPR applies, transfers are supported by lawful mechanisms as applicable, including adequacy decisions, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and relevant extensions, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), or other appropriate safeguards depending on the provider and transfer route.

Calendly states that user and invitee data are stored in U.S.-based data centres and that Calendly is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. Cloudflare and Google also publish information about DPF/SCC mechanisms and other international-transfer safeguards.

You may contact info@photon-digital.com to request further information about the transfer mechanism relevant to your data.

8. Retention

Prospect enquiries that do not become a client relationship: generally up to 24 months after the last meaningful interaction, unless we have a reason to keep them longer or delete them sooner.

Current/former client data, contracts, invoices and accounting records: for the duration of the relationship and afterwards for the period required by applicable tax, accounting or other law or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

Calendly booking data: for as long as needed to arrange the meeting and manage the related business relationship; Calendly may also retain data according to its own settings and privacy notice.

Google Analytics 4: user-level/event-level retention is governed by the GA4 property setting (Google provides 2- or 14-month options for standard properties). Aggregated reporting may remain available for longer. Cookie-specific expiry periods are shown in the Cookie Declaration.

Consent records: for as long as reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with consent requirements and according to CMP settings.

9. Security

We use reasonable technical and organisational measures proportionate to risk, including HTTPS/TLS, access controls, least-privilege access, multi-factor authentication where available, restrictions on access to client accounts, and reputable service providers with appropriate security measures.

No method of transmission or storage can guarantee absolute security.

10. Your rights

Depending on applicable law, you may have the right to obtain information and a copy of your data; correct inaccurate data; request deletion; restrict processing; object to processing based on legitimate interests; receive portable data where applicable; withdraw consent without affecting processing already lawfully carried out; and lodge a complaint with a competent supervisory authority.

To exercise your rights, email info@photon-digital.com. We may request the minimum additional information needed to verify your identity. Requests are handled within the time limits required by applicable law (under GDPR, normally within one month).

In Ukraine, you may complain to the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights or a court. Where GDPR applies, you may also complain to the supervisory authority in the EEA country of your habitual residence, place of work, or the alleged infringement.

11. Automated decision-making

Photon Digital does not make decisions about website visitors or people who contact us that are based solely on automated processing and produce legal or similarly significant effects within the meaning of GDPR Article 22.

12. Children’s data

Photon Digital is a business-to-business service and the website is not directed to children. We do not knowingly collect children’s personal data through the website. If you believe a child has provided us with personal data, please contact info@photon-digital.com.

13. Sale of personal data and marketing emails

We do not sell personal data. As of the date of this Policy, the website form is not used to subscribe visitors to a bulk marketing-email newsletter. If such communications are introduced, we will use an appropriate legal basis and provide an unsubscribe mechanism.

14. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy when our services, technology, vendors or legal requirements change. The current version will be published on this page with an updated “Last updated” date.
